newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: STRIKE CRIPPLES MELBOURNE TRANSPORT
Public transport in Melbourne is at a standstill this morning, and there are union threats of more industrial action.
Public trains, trams and buses have stopped until midnight.
There are additional private buses running free shuttle services between major carparks and the city centre.
An eight month dispute drags on, while unions demand a 10 per cent pay rise with little trade off, and the state government offers six per cent with productivity gains at six per cent.
Also, unions don't want capped redundancy which the government is planning to introduce during privatisation next year.
REYNOLDS SAYS SHE WILL NOT STAND FOR SENATE AGAIN
Queensland ALP Senator, Margaret Reynolds, has opened up speculation about her political future.
Her comments come as former Premier, Wayne Goss, ended speculation about his future, confirming that he will nominate for preselection for Pauline Hanson's seat of Oxley.
Senator Reynolds says she will not be standing for the Senate again, but says this will not spell the end of her political career.
"I am not running for the Senate again but that is all I will confirm. I do have a number of options that people are raising with me about what I may do after that time", Senator Reynolds said.
GOLD PRODUCERS WANT TO "EDUCATE" PM ABOUT GOLD INDUSTRY
Western Australian gold producers say they want a meeting with the prime Minister to educate him about the gold industry.
The Gold Industry forum, a committee of the Chamber of Minerals and Energy, says industry representatives had planned to meet Mr Howard during his Western Australian visit.
The visit was cancelled because of the Mr Howard's illness, and industry has now enlisted Premier Richard Court's assistance to organise a meeting with Mr Howard in the next few months.
Forum Chairman Peter Lalor says there is clearly no understanding of the industry at a federal level.
FRENCH PAIR SET FOR HOPMAN CUP
In tennis, Wimbledon runner-up Cedric Pioline will team with former Australian Open champion, Mary Pierce, at the Hopman Cup in Perth in January.
The French pair is the first team to confirm its attendance at the mixed teams tournament.
It is the second appearance at the Hopman Cup for both players.
Pearce is ranked 11th among the world's players and Pioline 23rd.
